checked_sources.source: Romano, Eckley, Fearnhead & Rigaill 2023, Fast Online Changepoint Detection via Functional Pruning CUSUM Statistics, arXiv:2110.08205
checked_sources.result: Primary-source verification. FOCuS exactly represents the all-window/all-change-size Page-CUSUM statistic using functional pruning. Exact naive implementations are O(n) per iteration/O(n^2) total; FOCuS has amortized O(1) update cost and expected O(log n) stored components/maximization cost, with the paper reporting about 15 quadratic evaluations around the millionth observation and <1 second for 10^6 observations on a common personal computer. This is model-specific Gaussian mean-change structure, not a theorem for general e-process detectors.

checked_sources.source: Romano, Eckley & Fearnhead 2023, A Log-Linear Non-Parametric Online Changepoint Detection Algorithm based on Functional Pruning, arXiv:2302.02718
checked_sources.result: Primary-source verification. NP-FOCuS uses functional pruning in a nonparametric online detector; pruning is average O(1) per iteration and expected retained curves are logarithmic in n under its Bernoulli trace assumptions. It supports the broader mechanism that exact/near-exact envelope pruning can replace explicit enumeration, but its threshold calibration and statistical guarantees are not the non-partitioned e-detector guarantees.

checked_sources.source: Shin, Ramdas & Rinaldo 2024, E-detectors: A Nonparametric Framework for Sequential Change Detection
checked_sources.result: Primary-source verification. E-SR/e-CUSUM mixtures preserve nonasymptotic ARL validity, while discrete parameter mixtures can be updated in O(K_alpha) time/space independent of n. The paper explicitly contrasts this with window-limited GLR and develops slowly growing/adaptive parameter mixtures. This removes parameter-adaptation cost as a necessary source of O(n) growth, but does not solve the newer unknown-baseline infimum/all-start computation.

checked_sources.source: Haddouche & Sakhi 2026, Sequential Off-Policy Learning with Logarithmic Smoothing, arXiv:2506.10664v2 / AISTATS 2026
checked_sources.result: Primary-source verification. Under adaptive/redeployed behavior policies, the main PAC-Bayes off-policy theorem is simultaneous over all update rounds k and all posterior Q, using a martingale/Ville argument, but the principal uniform theorem still assumes a data-independent prior P. Thus it directly covers adaptive logging plus adaptive posterior choice, but not the stronger same-stream data-dependent-prior frontier.

checked_sources.source: Haddouche & Guedj 2022, Online PAC-Bayes Learning, NeurIPS 2022
checked_sources.result: Primary-source verification from the published theorem text. Priors may form an F_{i-1}-measurable predictive sequence and posteriors may be data-dependent, without iid data. The guarantee controls cumulative conditional losses for a fixed horizon framework; it is not itself the same all-time adaptive-logging off-policy certificate supplied by the 2026 LS paper.

candidates_new.mechanism: For nonnegative all-start ARL/PFA e-detector aggregates, prune a deterministic/predictable subset of start-time terms and keep the same threshold. Because the pruned statistic is pathwise no larger than the full valid detector, its alarm time is no earlier; therefore the original false-alarm/ARL guarantee is conservatively preserved even if the pruned statistic is not itself proved to be an e-detector.
candidates_new.evidence_basis: Derived inference from the verified nonnegative start-time aggregation form in Saha & Ramdas 2026 plus threshold-validity logic; not stated as a theorem in the checked paper.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: Keeping only the most recent W start terms reduces the start-time dimension from O(t) to O(W) per update and O(NW) through horizon N, before accounting for the candidate-null infimum. False-alarm validity follows by pathwise domination D_pruned(t)<=D_full(t), hence tau_pruned>=tau_full under the same upper threshold.
candidates_new.scope: Conservative false-alarm/ARL preservation only. No generic detection-delay guarantee; if the informative post-change run must exceed W or the true changepoint's useful start is removed, delay can increase without a uniform bound.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Slow/small changes can be effectively forgotten; candidate-null optimization may still dominate computation; data-dependent pruning that is not monotone subset deletion needs a separate proof.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Use domination-safe pruning as a correctness-preserving emergency compute cap, not as the preferred fast path. Escalate W or disable pruning when detection evidence grows slowly.
candidates_new.confidence: high for validity inference; medium for practical usefulness

candidates_new.mechanism: Search for an exact functional-envelope/convex-hull representation of the all-start non-partitioned detector so dominated start candidates can be removed permanently, analogous to FOCuS rather than window truncation.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: FOCuS reduces an exact O(n)-per-step all-window statistic to expected O(log n) evaluation; update pruning is amortized O(1). The millionth Gaussian observation needs roughly O(10) retained quadratic pieces rather than 10^6 start candidates. NP-FOCuS obtains analogous logarithmic retained-function scaling under its Bernoulli-trace assumptions.
candidates_new.scope: Transfer hypothesis only for e-process families whose start-time/candidate-null objective admits a low-complexity envelope with certifiable dominance. No general theorem yet for arbitrary point-null e-processes or the inf_R operation.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Nonconvex/nonparametric candidate-null objectives may not admit exact dominance pruning; approximate pruning can silently alter delay or validity if it ever increases the statistic or discards a future-optimal component without proof.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Attempt structural pruning before settling for fixed windows: retain only starts/null candidates that remain on a certified upper evidence envelope, with exact equivalence or one-sided domination proof.
candidates_new.confidence: high that the mechanism works in source domains; medium-low for general non-partitioned e-detectors

candidates_new.mechanism: Separate two adaptation axes computationally: parameter/post-change-effect uncertainty can be handled by a fixed/slowly-growing discrete mixture with O(K) recursive updates, while start-time/unknown-baseline uncertainty gets its own pruning/envelope mechanism. Do not multiply both into one naive Cartesian all-history search.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: Their mixture e-SR/e-CUSUM updates have O(K_alpha) time and space independent of n and retain nonasymptotic ARL control. This shows adaptation over effect-size/tuning parameters need not force history-linear cost.
candidates_new.scope: Architecture decomposition. The unknown-baseline infimum in Saha & Ramdas 2026 remains unsolved computationally by this result.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: If the null-candidate dimension and effect-size mixture are strongly coupled, factorization can lose statistical efficiency or require a larger mixture grid.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Keep orthogonal uncertainty axes modular and recursively summarized; reserve expensive all-history computation only for the axis that provably requires it.
candidates_new.confidence: high for source mechanism; medium for transfer

candidates_new.mechanism: Treat predictable-prior online PAC-Bayes and adaptive-logging time-uniform off-policy PAC-Bayes as complementary but non-substitutable components. The former permits past-dependent priors; the latter gives all-k/all-Q off-policy validity but retains a data-independent prior in its main uniform theorem.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: Online PAC-Bayes allows F_{i-1}-measurable predictive priors and arbitrary data-dependent posterior sequences for cumulative conditional loss. Sequential LS proves with probability 1-delta a statement for all deployment rounds k and all Q under adaptive behavior policies using a fixed P.
candidates_new.scope: Negative/structural result: the checked primary theorems do not yet provide one theorem combining same-stream learned priors, adaptive logging, arbitrary stopping/time-uniformity, and simultaneous all-posterior off-policy validity.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Naively plugging Q_{k-1} in as the prior of the fixed-P off-policy theorem breaks the Fubini/martingale step unless a predictable-prior version is reproved with the importance-weighted process.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Until the combined theorem is found/proved, use a fixed audit prior for certification and a learned predictable prior only in the optimization/search layer, or pay an explicit independent adaptivity charge/split.

evidence_updates.update: Computational mitigation can be split into a conservative pathwise-dominated pruning fallback plus a higher-value search for exact functional-envelope pruning. This sharpens the previous generic O(N^2) blocker into a concrete safe fallback and a structural research target.

The source gap is now more precise: Online PAC-Bayes 2022 supplies predictable past-dependent priors but not the adaptive-logging off-policy all-time certificate; Sequential LS 2026 supplies adaptive logging plus all-k/all-Q validity but its main theorem uses a data-independent prior. The missing bridge is specific rather than generic.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Arbitrary functional pruning from FOCuS can be directly imported into non-partitioned e-detectors without proof.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not supported. FOCuS exactness relies on a piecewise-quadratic/convex-hull representation for Gaussian mean-change likelihoods; NP-FOCuS has its own Bernoulli-trace structure.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Require an exact envelope/dominance proof for the e-process family before pruning.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: A fixed recent-window truncation keeps first-order optimal detection delay generically.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: No. It preserves false-alarm validity by delaying alarms, but can delete the only start with enough accumulated post-change evidence.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Use only as conservative compute cap or with separately proved W-versus-information-rate conditions.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Adaptive off-policy PAC-Bayes 2026 already solves same-stream data-dependent priors.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: The main uniform theorem explicitly assumes a data-independent prior P.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Do not silently replace P with a learned prior in the certification theorem.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Online PAC-Bayes 2022 alone is a time-uniform adaptive-logging OPE theorem.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: No. It controls cumulative conditional losses with predictable priors in a general online framework, but does not supply the off-policy importance-weighted adaptive-logging certificate of the LS paper.
